functionality.rationale: The change is limited to native test target preprocessing, but an incorrect definition could prevent the affected tests from compiling.

security.rationale: The task does not change production code, credentials, cryptography, trust boundaries, or input handling.

performance.rationale: A preprocessor definition on test targets has no production runtime or resource impact.

compatibility.rationale: No public API, ABI, wire protocol, schema, or persisted format changes.

concurrency.rationale: No runtime synchronization, scheduling, or teardown behavior changes.

platform.rationale: The defect blocks the supported MSVC native matrix; a deterministic policy test covers the required target definitions on every development host.

persistence.rationale: The task does not read, write, migrate, or reinterpret persisted data.

adr.rationale: Defining NOMINMAX for existing test targets restores an established supported-platform build and creates no public or expensive-to-reverse decision.

architecture.rationale: The test targets remain in their existing session and transfer module boundaries; only their Windows preprocessing environment changes.

roadmap.rationale: This bugfix restores the existing CI platform contract and does not add or reschedule product behavior.

defect.symptom: The supported Windows native build fails while compiling session and transfer tests after production libraries compile successfully.
defect.expected_contract: The CI workflow requires native tests to compile on windows-2022, and shared native test support that consumes Windows headers must prevent SDK min and max macros from rewriting standard-library expressions.
defect.actual_behavior: MSVC reports C2589, C3878, C2760, and C2059 when Windows min and max macros expand std::min and std::numeric_limits::max expressions in session and transfer tests.
defect.trigger: Compile integrated delivery 549fd420bf6bc01168314ca8a58a0f720aa98638 with MSVC 14.44 in GitHub Actions run 31350356920.
defect.failure_fingerprint: FAILED: Windows native test support must isolate min and max macros
